name: H5N1 bird flu
value: Cattle-linked US cases; no human spread
summary: Recent US H5N1 cases in Yakima County were linked to infected cattle; ECDC finds no sustained human spread
state: ECDC's update of 9 Nov counts 74 US human H5 cases since April 2024 to 5 Nov, excluding the two most recent Yakima County, Washington, cases reported on 1 Nov, one of which was fatal (ECDC). It reports no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission. Searches to 15 Nov found no new human cluster, so these remain animal-to-human cases and the level stays Normal.
for_you: Risk to the general public remains low. Farm workers and people handling poultry, dairy cattle or wild birds are most exposed; UKHSA and Defra advise against touching sick or dead birds and to report them.
rubric_hit: Normal: sporadic animal-to-human cases only; no sustained human-to-human transmission (ECDC 9 Nov)

sources.title: ECDC — Avian influenza A(H5N1) human cases, United States, 2024–2026 (update 9 Nov)

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.

rubric.watch: Human clusters under investigation, rising human cases, or new mammalian species spread.
